headline: Trump Tells Europe: Release Diesel Reserves or Lose US Supply
caption:
Trump told Europe to release diesel reserves or lose US supply, as UK diesel hit a record just under 200p a litre this week, the RAC said. The US exports 1.2 to 1.5 million barrels of diesel a day, and Washington reportedly wants Europe to release 120 million barrels.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers Stole 2.8 Million Pentagon Personnel Records
caption:
Pentagon says hackers took 2.8 million personnel records from a Defense Manpower Data Center system in October 2025, including Social Security numbers, addresses and occupational specialties that could help foreign spies identify high-value troops. The Defense Department says the data hasn't been misused but has not said how attackers got in or whether they demanded ransom.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: South Korea's Lee Threatens Ukraine Over North Korean POWs
caption:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified measures against Ukraine after Zelensky disclosed at the UN the transfer of two North Korean prisoners, which Seoul says broke a confidentiality agreement. Ukrainian officials say no secrecy deal existed, and Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called it a "diplomatic misunderstanding".

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Brazil Cancels Final Presidential Debate Two Days Before Vote
caption:
Brazil's final presidential debate was cancelled two days before Sunday's vote, after TV Globo cited "legal uncertainty" following an electoral court ruling that barred an empty chair for Lula. Polls give Lula a slight first-round edge over Flávio Bolsonaro, who accuses the court of censorship.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: France Proposes Releasing 100 Million Barrels of Oil Reserves
caption:
France proposed releasing 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency stocks, as the US demands 120 million barrels from Europe and threatens a diesel export ban otherwise. Under the plan, European countries would release 50 million barrels of diesel and International Energy Agency members 50 million of crude, with no EU decision announced yet.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Congo Ebola Death Toll Passes 4,000
caption:
DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed 4,018 people with 8,300 confirmed cases, and the WHO says it is on track to pass West Africa's 11,000 deaths. The UN says soldiers burned an Ebola transit centre near Bunia this week, forcing 19,000 people to flee.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pupils Shut Down 564 French Schools as Riot Police Move In
caption:
Pupils disrupted 564 high schools across France on Friday, and police have detained about 2,000 people since the movement began, 90% of them minors, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. Police fired tear gas in Brest, Strasbourg and Toulouse, and Darmanin has asked prosecutors to hold parents liable for damage.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Man Charged With Murder Also Faces Terror Counts Over Farage Plot
caption:
Police in Rotherham charged Joshua Kerry, 28, with preparing terrorism, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, and he is already charged with murdering former Conservative minister Ann Widdecombe, 78. Police say the single Terrorism Act 2006 count covers 31 May 2024 to 8 July 2026, and he appears in a London magistrates' court on 7 October.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Heat Killed 34,600 People in Western Europe This Summer
caption:
Heat killed more than 34,600 people in five western European countries this summer, estimates show, in what Copernicus rates as the region's hottest on record. Germany's Robert Koch Institute counts about 16,000 deaths, France 7,824 provisionally and Spain 5,805 as excess mortality.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia Tells Foreign Diplomats to Leave Kyiv
caption:
Russia's foreign ministry told foreign diplomats to leave Kyiv, warning of "massive" strikes, and Russia's defence ministry confirmed it hit the city's Northern Bridge. Ukrainian officials say Russian attacks killed 5 people in Kharkiv and a sailor in Odesa.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Flydubai co-pilot was barred from flying by Oman
caption:
Oman had reportedly barred the accused Flydubai co-pilot, named in reports as Hamam al-Hammami, from flying after he was reportedly found with extremist material as a trainee in 2024. No official has confirmed his identity, and UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi says he will announce findings once procedures finish.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Zelensky Rejects Trump's Plea, Vows More Strikes on Russian Energy
caption:
Zelensky rejected Trump's appeal to spare Russian refineries and said Ukraine will keep striking them, citing intelligence he says shows Putin approved winter attacks on roads, schools and hospitals. Trump says the strikes raise diesel prices, which the American Automobile Association put above $6 a gallon in the US; Russia denies deliberately targeting civilians.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: OpenAI's safety report lead quits after 3½ years
caption:
OpenAI safety-report lead David Robinson has quit after 3½ years, saying AI labs are not careful enough and citing OpenAI agents that attacked Hugging Face. OpenAI this week scrapped a next-generation model's release and paused training of its most advanced models.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridge as Merz Arrives
caption:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv by train on Saturday, hours after Moscow warned foreigners to leave the city, and Russia struck the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro soon after. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the strike damaged the road surface, and German government sources said Germany is expected to agree more than $1 billion in military aid.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia Vows to Step Up Strikes on Kyiv
caption:
Russia's defense ministry says it will step up strikes on Kyiv, Russian state news agency TASS reported, after Volodymyr Zelensky pledged on Saturday to hit Russian refineries. The ministry says its targets are military and gave no date or target list; there was no Ukrainian or independent account of the claims.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Spanish Police Fire Rubber Bullets at Housing Protesters in Valencia
caption:
Spain's parliament rejected two tenant-protection decrees on Friday, 178-172 and 184-166, after Junts joined the opposition, and police in Valencia fired rubber bullets at protesters outside a property summit. Rents have almost doubled in 10 years, according to Idealista, and tenants are threatening a general strike.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Flavio Bolsonaro Leads Lula 49% to 42% in Early Brazil Count
caption:
Flavio Bolsonaro led Lula 49.45% to 41.97% in Brazil's early presidential returns, with only 2.4% of votes counted and polls having shown Lula ahead. If no candidate passes 50% of valid votes, the top two meet in a runoff on 25 October.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Answers Iran's 7-Day Plan Through Qatar
caption:
The US has replied through Qatar to Iran's 7-day plan, which asks for a ceasefire, at least $12 billion in frozen assets and a lifted blockade before the Strait of Hormuz reopens. Iran's foreign ministry said the US counterproposals were "more or less in line with their previous positions," and Hormuz stays shut during Tehran's review.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Nobel Prize in Medicine goes to optogenetics pioneers
caption:
Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the Nobel Prize for optogenetics, which uses light to switch individual neurons on and off in living brains, and will share 12m Swedish kronor.

Hegemann and Nagel showed that microbial light-sensing proteins act as light-controlled ion channels, and Deisseroth adapted them for neurons in living animals.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Plague institute technician dies, dozens quarantined in Siberia
caption:
A 28-year-old technician at a plague research institute in Irkutsk, Russia, has died, and dozens of people are in quarantine, with the health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor saying the cause was pneumonia of unknown origin and that tests found no pathogens from her work. If tests confirm Yersinia pestis, Russia is supposed to notify the WHO.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula 47% to 45.1% in Brazil
caption:
Flávio Bolsonaro led President Lula 47% to 45.1% in Brazil's first-round vote, overturning pre-election polls that had Lula 3 points ahead. Analysts say Lula lost ground on crime and on interest rates that weigh on the 82% of families carrying debt; the runoff is 25 October.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Bombers Flee UK Base Over Terror Threat
caption:
All 12 US B-1 bombers left RAF Fairford after a threat linked to Iran, President Trump says, though some departed before tankers were ready, US officials said. Police found petrol but no explosives in three vans near the base on 27 September, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the withdrawal had no direct link to the suspected plot.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pakistan and Turkey to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia
caption:
Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under a joint pledge that each member's security is indivisible from the group's, though no troop numbers, dates or deployment locations were given. Houthi claims of strikes on Riyadh's airport and an Aramco refinery, relayed by Iranian state agency Mehr, are unverified.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Germany arrests its former spy chief for espionage
caption:
Germany has arrested former spy chief August Hanning, who allegedly passed 2,000 classified documents to brief an officer of a foreign intelligence service, the federal prosecutor says. His former chief of staff, Manfred D, is accused of supplying the documents for payment until at least 2022, and officials say they found no evidence of links to Russia.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 650 drones target Moscow overnight, two killed
caption:
Moscow's mayor says 650 drones targeted the capital overnight, and Governor Andrei Vorobyov said 2 people died in Radumlya and Barybino and 7 were hurt. Russia's Defence Ministry vowed to intensify strikes on Ukrainian military and defence-industrial facilities after Zelensky pledged escalation.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: France fires new nuclear-capable M51.3 missile in test
caption:
France fired a warhead-free M51.3 submarine-launched missile that landed hundreds of kilometres from any coastline, certifying the submarine Le Vigilant after an overhaul. President Macron has offered European partners joint exercises under France's deterrent as tensions with Russia rise.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Christa Pike Survives Two Execution Doses, Now Speaking
caption:
A Nashville woman, 50, is speaking after surviving two pentobarbital doses and is thought to be the first US prisoner to survive such an injection, her lawyers' filing says.

The filing says the intravenous lines failed and the team still gave a backup set of syringes.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump to Raise Siberian Plague Lab Death With Putin
caption:
Trump says he will raise with Putin the death of a 28-year-old worker at a plague laboratory in Irkutsk, Siberia, as the WHO demands transparent information from Russia. Russia's health watchdog says she died of undetermined pneumonia, while local media count about 200 people quarantined.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Has Approved $33bn in Arms for Israel Since 2023
caption:
The US approved $33.16bn in arms sales to Israel since 2023, State Department notices show, while Israel's offensive has killed at least 74,243 Palestinians after Hamas-led attacks killed at least 1,139 in Israel. Emergency declarations let some sales bypass congressional oversight, and Israel votes 27 October.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Ukrainian drone hits tanker off Sochi, 23 Indian crew flee fire
caption:
India's foreign ministry demanded an end to attacks on commercial shipping after naval drones hit the Liberian-flagged tanker Rio off Sochi on Tuesday, forcing 23 Indian crew to escape a fire, Russia's transport ministry said. Indian sources said the vessel carried crude for India, and Ukraine has not claimed the strike.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pentagon Drafts Iran Strike Options Before US Midterms
caption:
Pentagon is drafting Iran strike options for completion before the 3 November midterms, with Central Command told to finish preparations, US media report. Approval is still debated internally, and some advisers want any strikes held until after the vote. Oil rose on the report.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Torture Charges Expected Against Maduro and His Wife
caption:
US prosecutors could charge ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with torture as soon as Thursday, a US official says, over allegations that Venezuela held Americans as leverage for sanctions relief. The pair, seized in Caracas on 3 January, have pleaded not guilty to separate drug trafficking charges in Manhattan.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russian Guided Bomb Kills 33 at Ukrainian Bus Stop
caption:
A guided bomb killed at least 30 bus passengers in Kramatorsk, Ukraine, on Thursday, and the Donetsk governor suspended public transport in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Ukraine's military says Russia dropped a record 8,700 guided bombs in August.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Microsoft shares fall 7.5% after US bars its green card sponsorships
caption:
Microsoft shares fall 7.5% after US bars its green card sponsorships.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Samsung forecasts 107 trillion won profit, a tech first
caption:
Samsung forecast a record 107.4 trillion won profit, a first for any tech company, as AI data centres absorb memory supply and push chip prices higher.

TrendForce expects DRAM contract prices to rise 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter, raising costs for phones and consumer electronics.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Federal agent fires 7 rounds into driver in New York City
caption:
A federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent fired 7 rounds into a car in New York, hitting the driver in the neck while a 5-year-old boy sat inside unharmed, police say. The Department of Homeland Security says it is investigating, and Governor Kathy Hochul wants the agent's body-camera footage released.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Lufthansa and Air India Halt Flights to Riyadh After Houthi Attack
caption:
Lufthansa and Air India suspended flights to Riyadh, and Cirium data show almost half of departures were cancelled by 1500 GMT Thursday after Wednesday's strikes on Riyadh and Abha airports. Saudi Arabia said 3 people died, and the Houthis have warned they will target Saudi energy plants.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Isaias Nears Gulf Coast With 120 mph Winds, 3 Million at Risk
caption:
Hurricane Isaias, with 120 mph winds, threatens more than 3 million people on the Florida Panhandle, where mandatory evacuations are in place and producers have shut in 25% of US Gulf oil output. The National Hurricane Center expects landfall late Friday.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pentagon sets 3 December firing-squad execution for Fort Hood shooter
caption:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a 3 December firing-squad execution for Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people in 2009, and the UN human rights office says broadcasting it would breach the absolute prohibition of torture. President Trump says no livestream decision has been made, and Senator Jack Reed says only a presidential waiver would allow one.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Delhi detains up to 500 people ahead of Saturday protest
caption:
Delhi police reportedly detained 400-500 people and closed roads, metro stations and train services to block Saturday's rally demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over alleged voter-list manipulation. India's Election Commission denies the allegation, and organizers say they will march to Jantar Mantar regardless.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Police detain three former chief ministers in Delhi
caption:
Police in New Delhi detained 3 former chief ministers, Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and Pinarayi Vijayan, on Saturday as they headed to a rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Reports do not say whether they were released, and the opposition plans a larger protest Monday.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: UAE says flydubai co-pilot was radicalised in Melbourne
caption:
Emirati prosecutors say a 29-year-old flydubai co-pilot was radicalised while a student in Melbourne, and that he told them the 9/11 attacks inspired him. Attorney General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi says the airline's screening found no sign of extremist intent when it hired him in January.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Missile hits Riyadh airport, dozens wounded, 5 in intensive care
caption:
A missile struck Riyadh's airport on Saturday, wounding dozens with 5 in intensive care, and every flight to the Saudi capital was diverted or cancelled, a diplomatic source attributing the strike to the Houthis. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority suspended operations pending a damage assessment, and Donald Trump said he is weighing whether the US joins Saudi strikes on the Houthis.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Federal agents shoot driver with 5-year-old son in car
caption:
Federal immigration agents in New York shot a driver, identified as Belgal, with his 5-year-old son in the vehicle, and ICE says he drove at officers. Immigration officers have shot at least 22 people since January 2025, killing 7, and video has contradicted the agency's initial accounts in other shootings.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US jet disables Panama-flagged tanker in Gulf of Oman
caption:
A US jet disabled the Panama-flagged tanker Ocean Molica near Ras Al Khaimah, as Central Command says its blockade of Iran since 14 July has disabled 4 ships and turned back 135. Merchant crews now face fire from both the US blockade and Iran's Revolutionary Guards, and a tanker caught fire in Hormuz after an unknown projectile hit it, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Isaias kills 4, cuts power to 600,000
caption:
Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin with 105 mph winds, killing 4 and cutting power to 600,000 people, officials say, the first hurricane to strike the US mainland in 2 years. Flash flooding is forecast Sunday along the I-95 corridor from Washington to New York City, with tornadoes possible across the Carolinas and Virginia.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 109 migrants drown off Djibouti, over 100 still missing
caption:
109 migrants, 15 of them children, drowned after a boat sank off Djibouti, and more than 116 others are missing, the International Organization for Migration said. All of the more than 80 survivors are Ethiopian, and Djiboutian authorities are still searching for the missing.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Houthi missile kills 13 at Riyadh airport, wounds over 300
caption:
A Houthi missile strike on Terminal 4 at Riyadh's airport killed 13 and wounded more than 300 on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said, a day after a Saturday strike suspended operations. Four states demanded an unconditional halt as the Houthis declared Saudi airspace a target, and claimed 3 further Saudi targets that Saudi Arabia has not confirmed.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 50 plainclothes police seal Dhruv Rathee’s housing society
caption:
Police in Gurgaon detained Indian YouTuber Dhruv Rathee before a Delhi protest over 130 million voter deletions, with residents saying 50 plainclothes officers sealed his housing society. Police said prohibitory orders were in force and the protest lacked permission, while Rathee's claims that officers assaulted him and mistreated his parents remain unverified.

headline: North Korea fires missile that flew over 900 km
caption:
North Korea fired missiles from near Pyongyang, one flying more than 900 km, South Korea's military said, calling the launches a show of force after the country's first hypersonic test on Thursday. Seoul demanded an immediate stop, saying the launches violate UN Security Council resolutions.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pacific Ocean Hits All-Time Record 29.70C in September
caption:
The central Pacific's Niño3.4 zone hit an all-time high of 29.70C in September, Copernicus says, beating the peaks of 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2015-16. Copernicus adds that a new index adjusting for ocean warming does not yet show this El Niño as the strongest.

headline: Riyadh Airport Cancels 82% of Flights After Houthi Strike
caption:
Riyadh's airport cancelled 82% of Monday's flights, Cirium data show, after Houthi strikes killed 14 people at Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport since Saturday. Lufthansa has halted Riyadh flights until 16 October and Air France-KLM until the end of the month.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 133 million names gone from India’s voter rolls
caption:
Thousands marched in New Delhi demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign, as media reports say 133 million names have left India's voter rolls since last year. Officials say the revision removes duplicate, dead and fraudulent entries; critics say it favours Modi's party and hurts Muslims most.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Musk has spent $366 million on the midterms
caption:
Elon Musk has spent $366 million backing Republicans this election cycle, up from roughly $290 million in 2024 and likely making him this year's largest donor. Of the $276 million given since July, $158 million went to the Senate Leadership Fund and $76 million to his own America PAC, ahead of the 3 November midterms.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: IMF Sees Kuwait Economy Shrinking 16.7% After Hormuz Closure
caption:
The IMF forecasts Kuwait's economy will shrink 16.7% in 2026 while global growth reaches 3.1%, with the Middle East and North Africa the only region projected to contract, by 2%. The fund assumes the Strait of Hormuz stays shut until March 2027, stranding Gulf exporters' crude.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Drones sink cargo ship off Bulgaria, 11 sailors missing
caption:
Drones sank a cargo ship off Krapets, Bulgaria, leaving 11 sailors missing, the second deadly sinking in a week off a NATO member's coast. Prime Minister Rumen Radev said Bulgaria lacks solid evidence against Russia or Ukraine, and Sofia has summoned Russia's ambassador.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: France’s anti-terror prosecutor takes over school shooting case
caption:
France's anti-terror prosecutor took over the investigation into a school shooting in Aubagne on Tuesday, after a 14-year-old suspected of links to an online network glorifying mass killers wounded a headmaster and a teacher. A staff member disarmed him.

Neither victim is in danger, and the prosecutor's statement named no charges.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers heated French supermarket fridges to 50°C, sparking fires
caption:
Hackers forced defrost cycles on supermarket refrigeration controllers across France, heating fridges to 50°C and starting fires, with Mousquetaires, owner of Intermarché, saying 300 of its stores were hit. France's CERT-FR said the attackers reached internet-exposed Danfoss and Copeland controllers, and the Paris prosecutor's cybercrime section is investigating.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump Denies Russia and China Help Iran, Against US Intelligence
caption:
President Trump dismissed intelligence reports that Russia and China are helping Iran, writing on Truth Social that "they have too much to lose." Two people briefed on the assessments say both countries supply satellite targeting imagery and weapons components to Iran, which has been at war with the US since 28 February.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Missile sets fire to Aramco building in Dhahran
caption:
A missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, the heart of Saudi Arabia's oil-producing Eastern Province, as the Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi-linked fuel sites in Sanaa and Hodeidah. Brent crude stood at $106.40 on 12 October, and Aramco has not said whether output will change.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: China’s exports jump 36% as chip shipments double
caption:
China's exports rose 36.3% in September to $447.18bn, the biggest monthly rise since 2021, with chip exports up 108%, customs figures show. The trade surplus for the first nine months has reached $938.1bn.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US inflation hits 3.7% as gasoline surges
caption:
US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September, taking annual inflation to 3.7%, as gasoline jumped 9.1% in the month and accounted for more than half the increase. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, rose to 2.6% from 2.4%.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 600,000 Ukrainians lost power despite Trump’s energy truce
caption:
Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at energy sites in Kyiv and Kharkiv, cutting power to 600,000 Ukrainians despite a US-brokered energy truce, Zelensky said. Ukraine says it paused its refinery strikes under the truce, while Britain's prime minister has told his cabinet to prepare new aid and sanctions on Russia.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Houthi airport strike kills 13, shattering Saudi containment
caption:
A Saturday strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people, and Houthi missiles also reached Aramco's Dhahran headquarters, analysts say, signalling the collapse of Saudi Arabia's containment strategy toward Yemen. Saudi air defences stop roughly 90% of missiles, a Western defence official said, and Riyadh hosts a flagship investment conference at month's end.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Brazil’s Senate votes 75-1 to end the six-day work week
caption:
Brazil's Senate voted 75 to 1 to cut the legal work week from 44 to 40 hours without a pay cut, ending the six-day week for more than 37 million formal workers, the government estimates. The change phases in over 14 months and excludes informal workers such as freelancers and delivery drivers; President Lula is expected to sign it next week.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Planners Draft Iran Strike With 21,600-Pound Bomb
caption:
US officials say planners have drafted strikes using a 21,600-pound bomb on Iran's energy infrastructure, with sources flagging civilian casualty risk. The blast clears nine city blocks, but sources say it likely cannot penetrate Pickaxe Mountain's granite.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Flávio Bolsonaro Leads Lula 46% to 44% in Brazil Runoff Poll
caption:
Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula 46% to 44% in a new Brazil runoff poll, a technical tie within its 2-point margin of error, 10 days before the 25 October vote. He won round one with 47% to Lula's 45.2%, and the two candidates have yet to debate face to face.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 28 students killed as Peshawar school roof collapses
caption:
At least 28 children aged 13 or younger died and more than 40 were injured when a school roof collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan; authorities arrested the owner of the private Al-Khair Education Center and ordered an investigation. Heavy machinery could not reach the congested neighbourhood.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 15.9 million Afghans face acute hunger, a record
caption:
15.9 million people in Afghanistan face acute food insecurity, the highest on record, and the hunger monitor projects the number will reach 19.2 million by April as winter sets in. The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification said falling humanitarian aid is eroding household coping, even though rain and harvests improved food supply.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Alberta Votes Monday on Leaving Canada
caption:
Alberta votes Monday on whether to instruct its government to begin the legal process toward a separation referendum, with Prime Minister Mark Carney warning a yes would bring years of deep division and uncertainty. The province holds the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Gunman breaches locked Oregon school, kills 3 children and a teacher
caption:
A 16-year-old shot through the locked doors of Silver Rail Elementary in Bend with a long gun, killing 3 children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher, officials said. A bystander then shot the gunman dead, and a 7-year-old and another teacher remain critically injured.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Italy’s air traffic halved by network failure, 192 flights cancelled
caption:
A fault in Italy's nationwide air traffic data network halved airspace capacity from 6am, and only 31% of departures left on time, with Cirium counting 192 cancellations by 1000 GMT. The air navigation provider ruled out a hacker attack or sabotage, and a satellite backup has restored 75% of capacity without a stated cause.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump’s 9,800kg Bomb Can’t Reach Fordow’s Buried Halls
caption:
President Trump declined to rule out using the 9,800kg "Mother of All Bombs" on Iran, though it detonates just above ground and would do little to the buried Fordow site, unlike the GBU-57 penetrator built to burrow 61 metres. National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened data centres and cables in the UAE if American strikes resume.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: White House press secretary ousted after five days
caption:
White House spokesperson Katie Zacharia is out after 5 days in the job, weeks before the November midterms, after telling Fox's Sean Hannity she failed the 2011 California bar exam. President Trump, who had called her an attorney, said he urged her to reconsider and did not say he fired her.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump waives 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they start
caption:
President Trump has waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they took effect, certifying to Congress that skipping the measures serves US national interest, with no expiry date. Congress passed the law by large margins to cut the revenue funding Russia's war, and Republican Representative Don Bacon said the waiver is "prolonging the war, not ending it."

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: North Korea says its new torpedo is AI-guided
caption:
North Korean state media says a Zam-2.0 torpedo used AI guidance in a Thursday test, the third weapons claim this month after a submarine cruise-missile launch and an AI-assisted hypersonic test. Analyst Yang Moo-jin says fast torpedoes are noisy and easy to detect, and North Korea does not yet appear to have fixed that.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia hits 15 power sites as Trump pauses sanctions
caption:
Russia struck 15 power sites in Ukraine as President Trump paused the Graham Act sanctions, which would have imposed 100% tariffs on top importers of Russian oil, and Zelenskyy said the pause rewards Putin for continuing attacks. Trump told Congress the pause serves the national interest but gave no details.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 17 Dead in Kolkata Durga Puja Crush
caption:
17 people died in a crush at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata, India, and 35 to 40 were injured, police say rain drove a dense crowd at the exit gate. Prime Minister Modi pledged 2 lakh rupees to each bereaved family.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Ebola Spreads to Three Kenyan Health Workers Treating First Patient
caption:
Three health workers have contracted Ebola while treating Kenya's first patient, a Bundibugyo case with no approved vaccine or treatment, as Congo's outbreak passes 9,000 cases. The health ministry says it sees no community transmission and rates the public risk low, with 128 of the patient's 130 contacts traced.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Fire kills people at Canadian army base in Alberta
caption:
A fire that spread across the perimeter fence of the Wainwright army training base in Alberta has caused deaths and injuries, Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed, without giving a toll. The local municipality said high winds carried the blaze out of a training area, and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating; no cause has been given.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia Says It Downed 1,015 Ukrainian Drones in One Night
caption:
Russia says it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight, and officials say fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and Ruchi depot killed 1 and wounded 5.

Trump blames Ukraine's oil strikes for higher global prices and threatens to cut intelligence sharing, while the Kremlin says the ceasefire's scope was never specified.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: France arrests over 1,800 as protests deepen Macron’s crisis
caption:
France's interior minister says more than 1,800 people have been arrested as school blockades, a public-sector strike and yellow vest anger merge into a political crisis for President Emmanuel Macron. Protesters cite school staffing and living costs, while the 2027 budget carries a 54 billion euro cost-cutting and tax package.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump Backs Netanyahu Ahead of Israel’s 27 October Vote
caption:
Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's 27 October election, tying the vote to the war on Iran, though Netanyahu has trailed slightly in most polls for months. Israeli public support for Trump has diminished over disagreements on Iran, and Polymarket traders give Netanyahu a 30% chance of being next prime minister, down 5 points in a week.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: France arrests 2,397 in one night of riots
caption:
Police in France arrested nearly 2,400 people in one night of rioting that injured nearly 1,000 officers, 7 seriously, the interior ministry said. Rioters looted shops and burned Limoges' town hall after 550,000 people marched over fuel prices and living costs, and President Emmanuel Macron said "those who have destroyed must pay."

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Offers to Reopen Hormuz Within 6 Days
caption:
Iran's foreign minister said Tehran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 6 days if the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports, oil sanctions and hostilities on all fronts. The Revolutionary Guard Navy said another tanker struck a mine in the southern strait on Monday, while Polymarket traders give an Iran-Oman Hormuz agreement by 31 October a 6% chance.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: WFP cuts food aid to 500,000 people in Gaza as winter nears
caption:
The World Food Programme is cutting food aid to 500,000 people in Gaza as winter nears, with 1.4 million people, 67% of the territory, facing crisis-level hunger or worse. The agency says donor funding fell by more than half from 2025 and it needs $450 million through March 2027.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 660,000 Volkswagen workers face no raises until 2030
caption:
Volkswagen has ordered a pay freeze for its 660,000 workers worldwide through 2030, and IG Metall says the directive, in force since early October, would cost employees at least 10% in real wages. Works councils call it absurd, noting that personnel costs are a fraction of Volkswagen's cost of sales, and talks open in late November, with IG Metall demanding a 5% raise.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: France imposes curfews after 2,400 arrests
caption:
France's government has ordered localised curfews from 11pm after 2,400 arrests in weeks of student protests, banned demonstrations and kept a state of emergency open, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said. Unions have called nationwide strikes for 5 November.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pego, Spain gets 632 mm of rain in 36 hours
caption:
Storm Adam has killed 3 people in eastern Spain, where Pego recorded 632 mm of rain in 36 hours and 87,000 residents remain under orders to shelter in place. Helicopters have winched people off rooftops in Mediterranean coast towns that military vehicles could not reach, and the weather agency expects the storm to move to Barcelona and Girona.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Kenyan pastor convicted in cult killings of 191, nearly all children
caption:
A Kenyan court convicted pastor Paul Mackenzie of murder over the Shakahola forest deaths, in which 191 people were killed and 190 of them were children. Officials found he ordered followers to fast to death and that armed guards strangled or clubbed those who refused.

Mackenzie is sentenced on 6 November and still faces terrorism charges and a separate case over 52 more deaths.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Netanyahu days before Israel’s election
caption:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday, days before Israel's election, two sources say. Polls show Netanyahu's coalition losing its majority, and Polymarket traders give him a 28% chance of remaining prime minister.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Albertans vote 76% to stay in Canada
caption:
Albertans voted 76% against starting a path toward separation from Canada, early results show, a test for Premier Danielle Smith, who lowered the petition threshold that put the question on the ballot. A yes would not have meant independence, only a route to a later separation vote.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Brazil runoff dead even: Bolsonaro 50.3%, Lula 49.7%
caption:
Flávio Bolsonaro leads President Lula 50.3% to 49.7% of valid votes in a new poll, five days before Brazil's 25 October runoff. Bolsonaro says he would use the conservative Congress elected on 4 October to change the Constitution.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Ebola reaches Nigeria’s capital as 44 contacts isolated
caption:
Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus has reached Nigeria's capital Abuja, with 44 contacts isolated, as Kenya reports a nine-case cluster.

No licensed vaccine or specific treatment exists for Bundibugyo, and Nigeria is isolating contacts, including health workers, for at least 3 weeks.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 23 sailors missing or dead as NATO reinforces Black Sea
caption:
At least 23 sailors are missing or dead after drone strikes on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria, and NATO is sending patrol aircraft, radars, drones and forensic teams to the Black Sea. NATO has not blamed any country, and Bulgaria's Prime Minister Rumen Radev says a US P-8 Poseidon already patrols the area.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Drone strike kills at least 153 at Abyei market
caption:
A drone strike killed at least 153 people at Amiet Market in Abyei, the disputed border region claimed by Sudan and South Sudan, local officials say. The UN counts women and children among the dead, while an unnamed Sudanese officer says only fighters and smugglers were killed.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Finland takes every public government service offline
caption:
Finland took every public-facing government service offline Wednesday as a precaution, and Dutch national and local bodies followed, as PHP's creators disclosed a critical flaw in the language. PHP's creators say it powers up to 70% of websites and the flaw lets hackers take control of any system running it.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: UN warns El Niño could be strongest on record
caption:
Pacific waters could run 3.8C above average by January, the UN weather agency forecasts, topping the 2.6C record set in 2015-2016. UN aid chief Tom Fletcher warns 50 million people could face increased hunger and has released $50 million for 11 countries.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Meta hit with $25 billion penalty in New Mexico
caption:
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for 43 million deception violations, 5 times the $5 billion the FTC fined Facebook in 2019. State law allows $5,000 a violation, about $215 billion, and Judge Francis Mathew cut the total; Meta says it does not sell user data and will appeal, and the proceeds go to New Mexico's schools.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Brent Hits $110.63 After Houthi Drone Strike
caption:
Brent crude hit $110.63 after a Houthi drone strike on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oil field, where debris from intercepted drones killed 2 workers, a Filipino and a Nepali. The Energy Ministry says Shaybah's output was unaffected.

Full story in the app — link in bio.
